text:
Noah: hey all, finishing my first PR and want to confirm the repo norms quick: branch naming, commit subject, and label expectations?
Priya: welcome! branch: feature/<ticket>-short-desc or fix/<ticket>-short-desc. if no ticket: feature/add-thing. keep it <= 50 chars after the slash.
Samir: commit subject: imperative, small scope: e.g., "feat(cache): add LRU per-user cache". Use conventional-ish scopes but it's not enforced.
Noah: PR size? when do we split work into multiple PRs?
Priya: try to keep PRs reviewable: under ~300 changed lines ideally. If it's large, split by logical parts (api contract, impl, tests). Include a short changelog note if user-visible API changes.
Samir: reviewers: request 1 reviewer for normal changes. For infra/runtime/public APIs request 2 and add @infra-team or check CODEOWNERS. CODEOWNERS will auto-request but manual ping helps.
Noah: labels and CI?
review-bot: auto-labeler: applies size/* based on diff and detects PR type (feat/fix/chore) by title. Required checks: lint, unit, secret-scan, build-image.
docs-bot: PR template link: https://redwood.internal/dev/pr-template. Fill out Summary, Test Plan, Rollout, and Owners. If you add a feature flag, include a cleanup task.
Priya: tests: unit tests required for logic. For anything touching infra or containers add a small integration smoke test. Avoid huge e2e in PR.
Samir: secret mishap? rotate rotated keys, remove from history with interactive rebase, force-push with --force-with-lease, and note in PR "history rewritten to remove secret".
Noah: do we squash?
Priya: keep iterative commits while developing, but tidy history before merge. Squash into logical commits per feature. If reviewers ask to preserve history, keep and clean messages with rebase.
Noah: thanks! I'll open as draft until CI passes and then request reviews with a short list of focus areas.
Samir: one last tip: include small reproduction steps and any perf numbers if relevant; it speeds reviews. welcome aboard! :tada:
